subject: Shiny Server - Is sky the limit?

messages.author: 2ef256a129b97763
messages.subject: Shiny Server - Is sky the limit?
parts:
Hi

On the back of a successful Shiny App for around 10 users on an intranet, I'm thinking to potentially use Shiny for a web app, potentially available for users "in the hundreds".

If I understand this correctly, Shiny Server creates a "full" environment for each user. Possibly this means that  the obvious limit to the number of users will be the available RAM, e.g. if I have 128GB and my app environment takes say 1 GB (and leaving something for the OS), could I have > 100 users?

What if I would need 1,000 users? Or more?  Should I just think of using another technology or these numbers could be viable (taking a set of precautions of course)?

If I could create any number of AWS instances where to install the same application, could I imagine to just distribute the load with elastic load balancing?

Also, I understand that Shiny Server professional is limited to a pre-defined number of users.  Is it a purely licensing issue? Any volume discount foreseen?

Thanks

Enzo

I think I have a more clear understanding on the scalability on a single server / multi-core machine.

I am still unclear on memory management (is one "memory space" per user or else?).  Also, would Shiny-Server Pro work with AWS in a multi-instance environment and elastic load balancer?

Thanks

Enzo

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Shiny Server - Is sky the limit?
parts:
Hi Enzo,

Memory wise, on Shiny Server Open Source it is one R process per app, and that one process can potentially serve many users. Whether objects are duplicated for each user or shared across users depends on where you define them; see this article for details:
http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/scoping.html

With Shiny Server Pro it is the same except you're not limited to one R process per app. Each of the multiple R processes per app can serve many users.

Yes, Shiny Server Pro (and Open Source for that matter) work with AWS and ELB. Make sure you enable sticky sessions in ELB.
